A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 3 – Teacher’s Notes

   Description

In this activity students focus on key vocabulary in the question and multiple-choice answers. They
scan read the text to find the answer and then read again more thoroughly to make sure the other
answers are incorrect. Finally, they are given the rest of the sample task from the exam to complete within
a set time.

Time required:  20 minutes

Materials        Student handout
required:        Follow-up activities (optional)

Aims:            to familiarise students with A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 3
                 to practise skim reading for general understanding
                 to practise reading for detailed information

Procedure

    1. Explain to students that they will be doing Part 3 of the A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing
         exam. The text has different members of a family mentioned and may be confusing for some
         students. Review the target vocabulary by drawing a family tree on the board

   Use this as an opportunity to talk about family; ask students questions about their families and
        review key adjectives and vocabulary. An example of a family tree is shown below.

                              grandmother and grandfather (grandparents)

                mother (wife) and father (husband)

                                                 daughter and son (children)

2. Give your students Handout 1. Ask them to read the text quickly. How many members of a
            family do we learn about in the text? Ask them to read, underline and write down the names of
            the family members in their notebooks. Allow them to check their answer with their partner
            before open class feedback (see Answer key).

         3. Write the words: dancer, teacher, dressmaker on the board. Ask your students to describe each
              job with their partner before taking whole class feedback. Possible answers:
                  a dancer – performs on stage to music
                  a teacher – teaches you something/helps you to learn
                  a dressmaker – makes clothes

         4. Write question 14 on the board ‘What is Alice Watson’s job now?’ Refer back to the words on
              the board. Is she a dancer, a teacher or a dressmaker? Ask the class to read the text again
              quickly and decide on the answer. Allow them to check their answer with their partner before
              open class feedback (answer is B: a teacher). Elicit from your students how they got the
              answer:

                  these days = now
                  gives ballet lessons = teaches
                  was a doctor = not now, in the past

           Explain how the text never has the same vocabulary as the questions so it is important to look
           at the whole paragraph as there maybe more information after the first sentence.

         5. Ask your students to complete questions 15–18 from the handout on their own. Remind them
              to read the whole paragraph before making their decision. Set a time limit of 10 minutes.
              Allow them to check their answers with their partner before open class feedback. While
              monitoring the pairs, you will hear what problems they may have had with any vocabulary
              which you can address on the spot and then to the whole class.

         6. Elicit the answers from your students explaining any vocabulary necessary from your
              monitoring (see Answer key).

Suggested follow-up activities:

    1. Ask students to draw their own family tree and write about people in their family.

If you want the students to practise using the answer sheet, photocopy it and ask students to fill in the
lozenges in pencil for their answers to Part 3.
